correctness.rationale: For n>=3, incidences i--s_ij encode directed arcs i->j. Two distinct chosen arcs conflict iff nonreciprocal and they form a length-two directed walk with three distinct old vertices, because this creates a three-edge path whose outer edges are selected. A reciprocal pair i<->j excludes any further incidence at i or j, so such pairs are vertex-disjoint. Remaining arcs must run from sources to targets with no vertex both a head and tail. Inclusion-maximality forces every old vertex to be used, every source-target arc present, and excludes the single 1x1 block since its reverse remains feasible; without block, reciprocal pairs must be perfect or near-perfect. The disjoint structural census yields n!/(2^c c!a!u!) for c reciprocal pairs and complete a-by-u block, plus perfect/near-perfect pairings. Size 2c+au=n-1+(a-1)(u-1) and maximum floor(n²/4); odd n implies even sizes. Raw 3-edge-path bridge tests and exhaustive subset enumeration independently reproduce n=3:9z², n=4:8z³+9z⁴, n=5:85z⁴+20z⁶. Finite test not universal proof.
